title: Field install — Lighthouse knots weekly memo
content:
Weekly standup notes + action log for Lighthouse Health (on-prem cluster + VPC egress tunnel) — week of 2028-03-21

Context: customer is mid-install of a 3-node on-prem bundle (2x A2 + 1x control) with a separate VPC egress tunnel for model telemetry. Customer is in the EU region and has unusual network stack (BMC + isolated management VLAN). Goals this week were: finish NFS tuning, validate KMS/HSM integration, and stabilize KV cache persistence across node reboots.

Summary of current state:
- Core install: control plane up; inference nodes boot but runtime frequently OOMs on long requests.
- Networking: inter-node MTU mismatch discovered (customer management VLAN NATs 1400). We see packet fragmentation causing >200ms tail latency on KV sync.
- Storage: NFS mount on /var/lib/redwood served by vendor NAS using async write. Observed rare IO stalls during model warmup.
- Security: KMS handshake fails intermittently (TLS parent cert chain incomplete on customer's internal CA).
- Observability: agent-heartbeat gaps align with NFS stalls and occasional kubelet restarts.

Daily notes
- Mon 03/21 standup (remote):
  - Noted MTU symptoms after large-batch inference test #7. Arjun reproduced fragmentation locally by simulating MTU 1400 on a test network.
  - Priya ran quantized model smoke: memory behavior nominal; long-sequence tests push transient peak memory to 95% due to prefetch buffer sizing.
  - Action: Maya to coordinate with customer netops to schedule a short maintenance window to test jumbo frames/MTU normalization.

- Tue 03/22 on-site triage with customer (3h):
  - Performed tcpdump capture at kernel and switch level. Confirmed that IP fragments were reassembled on CPU causing CPU steal and latency spikes.
  - Raised immediate mitigation: change inference node kernel sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1 to avoid PMTU blackhole for now (temporary).
  - Filed JIRA PD-4923: "MTU mismatch -> KV sync tail latency" (Arjun owner).
  - Ran safe-mode model run with smaller batch size and reduced prefetch window; reduced OOM events in trial.

- Wed 03/23 escalation to SRE and Security: 
  - KMS/TLS: customer CA sent only leaf+intermediate, missing root anchor in chain; Java-based KMS client rejected chain intermittently depending on TLS library.
  - Security recommends rotating to pre-shared test key for install completion then swap to KMS after proper CA chain is provisioned.
  - Action: Lena to draft secure temporary key rotation procedure and logging to satisfy compliance while chain is fixed. ETA EOD Thu.

- Thu 03/24 afternoon:
  - NFS root cause narrowed: vendor NAS configured async_commit by default for performance; under simultaneous small-file workloads the commit jitter causes heavy fsync stalls.
  - Workaround: mount with sync and set rsize/wsize conservative values; re-test shows stable KV checkpointing but write throughput drops ~18% (acceptable for now).
  - Action: Arjun to open installer PR to add conservative NFS mount flags for our installer when host shows vendor NAS fingerprint (PR: installer/pull/412).

- Fri 03/25 wrap and customer sync:
  - Customer ran 12-hour soak with adjusted MTU sysctl and NFS mount changes; observed mean latency reduction 22% and no OOMs in that window.
  - KMS still blocked; customer security team agreed to provide root cert by Mon 03/27.
  - Next steps agreed: swap to full KMS once cert chain provided; evaluate restoring async NFS if vendor patches firmware.

Open blockers and risks
- KMS certificate chain (blocking): prevents us from enabling customer-managed KMS end-to-end. Compliance requires hardware-backed key usage; temporary PSK approach needs exec approval from customer security.
- Firmware update dependency (vendor NAS): customer hesitant to firmware patch without longer maintenance window — leaves us on sync mounts with perf hit.
- Kernel parameter differences across nodes: some nodes had vm.max_map_count set to 65530 vs recommended 262144 -> increases mmap churn for large models. Need centralized sysctl enforcement in installer.
- BMC/OOB management VLAN: bumped into IP collisions when tools probe; request customer to isolate management traffic during install windows.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Arjun Singh: PD-4923 open + installer PR to add NFS conservative flags (link above). ETA 2028-03-28.
- Maya Rodriguez: coordinate customer netops for MTU normalization test & confirm BGP/route policy for VPC tunnel. ETA 2028-03-27.
- Lena Kovacs: temporary KMS rotation runbook draft for customer security review. ETA 2028-03-24 (in-flight).
- Priya Menon: run extended memory profiling for long-sequence generation with current prefetch window and provide tuned defaults. ETA 2028-03-30.
- Evan Chen: propose installer sysctl enforcement RFC and small config layer tweak to pin vm.* and net.* recommended values. ETA 2028-04-02.

What went well
- Cross-team coordination: SRE + security + on-call infra engaged quickly during Tue escalation.
- Quick mitigations: MTU sysctl and NFS mount flags produced measurable improvement within 24 hours.
- Telemetry alignment: tcpdump + agent traces allowed tight correlation between IO stalls and node restarts.

Notes to self / unresolved questions
- Need a way in installer to fingerprint vendor NAS model (serial/string in /proc/mounts?) to auto-choose mount flags. Could be fragile across vendors.
- Should we add an install-time KMS test that validates full chain (including root) before switching to production keys?
- Consider a small onprem acceptance test suite that runs a long-sequence gen for 30 minutes to catch memory/fork-related OOMs pre-handoff.

Next week priorities
- Complete PRs and RFC for sysctl enforcement (Evan + Arjun).
- Lock customer on maintenance window for firmware if they accept vendor patch risk; else prepare perf report for sync mount penalty (Maya).
- Finish memory profiling and recommend prefetch/window defaults (Priya).
- Revisit KV checkpoint logic to add backoff and jitter on heavy NFS stall patterns (engineering spike).

Appendix: Quick troubleshooting commands used this week
- tcpdump -i bond0 -s 0 -w /tmp/mtu-frag.pcap host 10.2.1.7 and port 12345
- watch -n 1 'cat /proc/net/snmp | grep TcpExt' (to spot reassembly stalls)
- mount -o remount,sync,rsize=65536,wsize=65536 server:/export/redwood /var/lib/redwood
- openssl s_client -showcerts -connect kms.internal:443 -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/customer-root.pem

Slack refs / Links
- slack:#private-deploy: thread "lighthouse: mtu+nas" (see pinned captures)
- confluence:private-deploy/lighthouse-onprem-runbook (template / acceptance checklist)

End of memo — will iterate on Monday after customer provides root cert and netops confirms maintenance slot.
